notes: The 10k pull-down resistor connects pin 4 (column 6) to the ground rail; the button's other side (column 8) goes to 5V via the rail.
In the image the lower half of the breadboard is labelled rows a-e and the upper half f-j. I followed the catalogue naming literally: rows a-e are bank 't' and rows f-j are bank 'b'.
Exact rail hole numbers (bn.1, bp.2, bn.5, bp.7) are estimated from the image. The bottom rail's upper line is treated as the ground (-) rail and the lower line as the 5V (+) rail.
The USB cable is not drawn in the circuit image but is needed to power and program the Leonardo, so it is included.
The schematic shows the input on pin 2 but the text and the circuit image use pin 4, so pin 4 is used.
Button legs: column 6 is side 1 and column 8 is side 2. Each column has one leg on each side of the centre gap.
